called the Future Circular Collider, which could follow the Large Hadron Collider in the 2040s.

Most fundamental particles have a corresponding antiparticle – another sub-atomic particle that has the same mass but a different

charge. FCC-ee would accelerate electrons and their corresponding antiparticles (known as positrons) around a 91km-long ring underneath the French-Swiss border, before colliding the two beams of particles inside

. These detectors are specialised experiments that can track and measure the particles produced when the beams crash into one another.

FCC-ee has a key advantage over proton-proton colliders such as the Large Hadron Collider:

together electrons and positrons can directly produce a Higgs boson. By looking for this process, we can probe the strength of the electron-Higgs interaction.

Detecting new particles

In principle, the measurement is simple: collide electrons with positrons and
the Higgs bosons produced. In practice, it is very challenging. To produce enough Higgs bosons, the collider would need to run for a few years at an energy

close to the mass of the Higgs boson particle.

However, that’s a long time to run this machine in such a specialised way. The measurement also relies on us knowing the Higgs mass much more precisely than we do today. Detecting the Higgs bosons is another challenge, because many

processes can mimic the desired signal.

In a recent preprint (which has not yet been published in a peer-reviewed journal) on this topic, a team of physicists assumed that the Higgs bosons decay (or

) into W bosons, another fundamental particle with a lower mass. They used a machine learning algorithm to distinguish the desired signal from other processes. In simulations, they found that this approach could improve
to the electron-Higgs interaction by nearly a factor of 200 compared with current limits at the Large Hadron Collider.

reading.title: 主旨、理解与信息定位
reading.instruction: 阅读原文后回答 5 道选择题：1 道主旨、1 道内容理解、1 道段落细节、2 道信息定位。段落细节题以题干指定段落为准。

questions.prompt: Which statement best summarises the overall focus of this article?
options: Bacteria-infecting viruses may offer new ways to tackle antibiotic resistance.
Chemical evidence in ancient rocks helps scientists date the beginnings of plate tectonics.
Aboriginal astronomical knowledge explains celestial movements and their connections to life on Earth.
A new CERN experiment could deepen understanding of the electron and fundamental physics.
questions.explanation: 把标题与全文各段的中心内容连起来判断主旨，避免把同一主题下的其他话题当成本文重点。
questions.evidence: The current best theory to explain fundamental physics, known as the Standard Model, offers no explanation for this.

questions.prompt: What proposed facility could test the physics discussed in the article?
options: A collider at CERN in Geneva
questions.explanation: 第 4 段提供了作答依据。正确选项用不同说法表达了文中的信息；请比较范围、数量、因果关系与限定词。
questions.evidence: But a proposed collider at Cern, in Geneva, could finally put that to the test.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is explicitly made in paragraph 10?
options: The mass of the electron is very small, contributing little to the mass of the atom, but it is vital for determining an atom’s size.
These detectors are specialised experiments that can track and measure the particles produced when the beams crash into one another.
By looking for this process, we can probe the strength of the electron-Higgs interaction.
Six are called quarks and include the “up” and “down” quarks that make up protons and neutrons.
questions.explanation: 定位第 10 段，比较四个选项的具体信息。其余选项来自本文其他段落，并非本段明确陈述的内容。
questions.evidence: Six are called quarks and include the “up” and “down” quarks that make up protons and neutrons.

questions.prompt:
Which paragraph contains the following information?
“Most fundamental particles have a corresponding antiparticle – another sub-atomic particle that has the same mass but a different electric charge.”
questions.explanation: 这句话位于第 17 段。先找关键词，再核对上下文；正文页显示相同的段落编号。
questions.evidence: Most fundamental particles have a corresponding antiparticle – another sub-atomic particle that has the same mass but a different electric charge.

“However, new theories could modify interactions between the electron and the Higgs field, including through the action of previously undiscovered particles.”
